plan.contextChunk: This figure is a single labeled diagram of an upward-opening parabola drawn on a Cartesian coordinate plane, with thin black arrowed axes crossing near the lower left of the curve and marked x at the right and y at the top. The parabola is a heavy dark blue curve whose two branches end in arrowheads pointing up and outward. Its lowest point is a filled dark blue dot above the horizontal x-axis, connected by a short leader line to the label Vertex at the left. A dashed orange vertical line rises through that dot and carries the orange label Axis of symmetry at the upper right. Directly above the vertex on that same vertical line sits a small teal dot labeled Focus in teal. A short dashed blue horizontal segment runs through the teal dot from one branch of the curve to the other and is tagged Latus rectum by a curved arrow from the upper left. Below the vertex, a dashed red horizontal line spanning the width of the frame is labeled Directrix in red, and the x-axis lies lower in the frame. Color-coding the four named features separately lets the reader see that the axis of symmetry meets the directrix at a right angle and that the vertex lies midway between focus and directrix. The drawing establishes the vocabulary used to define a parabola as the set of points equally distant from the focus and the directrix.

interactionPlan.concept: A parabola is the set of all points equidistant from a fixed point (the focus) and a fixed line (the directrix), with the vertex, axis of symmetry, and latus rectum naming the key parts of that construction.
elements: thin black x-axis with arrowheads at both ends, labeled 'x' at right
thin black y-axis with arrowheads at both ends, labeled 'y' at top
heavy dark-blue upward-opening parabola with arrowheads on both branches
filled dark-blue vertex dot at the lowest point of the curve, above the x-axis
black leader line from the vertex dot to the label 'Vertex' on the left
dashed orange vertical line through the vertex spanning the figure height
orange label 'Axis of symmetry' at the upper right of that dashed vertical line
small teal focus dot on the axis of symmetry, above the vertex
teal label 'Focus' to the right of the focus dot
short dashed light-blue horizontal segment through the focus, spanning from one branch to the other (latus rectum)
curved black arrow from the label 'Latus rectum' (upper left, blue text) to the dashed light-blue segment
dashed red horizontal line below the vertex spanning the frame width (directrix)
red label 'Directrix' at the right end of the dashed red line
construction-view only: movable sample point P on the parabola
construction-view only: teal segment from P to the focus labeled with its length
construction-view only: red perpendicular segment from P straight down to the directrix, with a small right-angle square at the foot
construction-view only: matching tick marks / 'equal' annotation showing the two segments have the same length

interactions.label: Focus–vertex distance p
interactions.teaches: The single parameter p sets the shape: as the focus rises and the directrix drops by the same amount, the parabola opens wider; as p shrinks, the curve tightens around the axis. The vertex always stays halfway between focus and directrix, and the latus rectum is always 4p wide.

interactions.label: View
interactions.teaches: The vocabulary diagram and the defining property are the same picture: the named parts exist because every point on the curve is equally far from the focus and the directrix.

interactions.label: Point P along the parabola
interactions.teaches: Sliding P anywhere on the curve keeps the two distances equal — the equality is not a coincidence at one spot but the rule that generates every point of the parabola, including the vertex where both distances equal p.

Each vocabulary term — vertex, focus, directrix, axis of symmetry, latus rectum — attaches to one specific object, and hovering isolates it with its own construction lines instead of reading five labels at once.

demo_steps.title: The named parts
demo_steps.narration: Start with the standard labeled parabola: a dark blue curve, its vertex, the teal focus above it, the red directrix below, the orange axis of symmetry through both, and the dashed latus rectum across the focus. Hover any feature to light it up alone.

demo_steps.title: Why equidistant?
demo_steps.narration: Switch to the distance construction. A point P on the curve grows a teal segment to the focus and a red perpendicular segment down to the directrix — and they are exactly the same length.

demo_steps.title: It holds everywhere
demo_steps.narration: Slide P along the curve. The two segments change length together but never differ — this equality is the definition of the parabola, not a special case.

demo_steps.title: The vertex is the midpoint
demo_steps.narration: Move P to the bottom. Both distances shrink to the same value p: the vertex is the one point sitting halfway between focus and directrix, on the axis of symmetry.

demo_steps.title: Changing p reshapes the curve
demo_steps.narration: Increase p: the focus climbs, the directrix drops the same amount, and the parabola opens out wide with a latus rectum of width 4p.

demo_steps.title: A tight parabola
demo_steps.narration: Shrink p and the focus and directrix squeeze toward the vertex, pinching the curve into a narrow channel — same definition, different single parameter.

interactionPlan.keyInsight: Every point on a parabola is the same distance from the focus as from the directrix — the vertex is simply the point where that shared distance is smallest, which is why it sits exactly halfway between them.
interactionPlan.reconstructionNotes: Cartesian plane with thin black arrowed axes, origin low and left of center; 'x' at the right end of the horizontal axis, 'y' at the top of the vertical axis. A heavy dark-blue (#1f4e79-ish) upward-opening parabola fills the upper portion with arrowheads on both branches. Its vertex is a filled dark-blue dot sitting noticeably above the x-axis, with a short black leader line to a left-side label 'Vertex'. A dashed vertical orange line passes through the vertex from top to bottom of the frame, labeled 'Axis of symmetry' in orange near the top right of the line. A small teal dot on that line a short way above the vertex is labeled 'Focus' in teal to its right. A dashed light-blue horizontal chord through the focus stretches from one branch to the other; a curved black arrow points to it from the blue label 'Latus rectum' at the upper left. Below the vertex, a dashed red horizontal line spans the full frame width and is labeled 'Directrix' in red at its right end, positioned between the vertex and the x-axis. Keep vertex-to-focus and vertex-to-directrix gaps visually identical. In the 'Distance construction' view, dim the text labels, place a highlighted point P on one branch, draw a teal straight segment P→focus and a red vertical segment P→directrix with a small right-angle marker at the directrix, mark both with equal tick marks and an '=' callout, and show small 'p' brackets between vertex-focus and vertex-directrix. Hover should brighten the chosen feature and gray the others.

authoredContext:
In Quadratic Functions, we learned about a parabola’s vertex and axis of symmetry. Now we extend the discussion to include other key features of the parabola. See the figure. Notice that the axis of symmetry passes through the focus and vertex and is perpendicular to the directrix. The vertex is the midpoint between the directrix and the focus.

The line segment that passes through the focus and is parallel to the directrix is called the latus rectum. The endpoints of the latus rectum lie on the curve. By definition, the distance d from the focus to any point P on the parabola is equal to the distance from P to the directrix.

Key features of the parabola

This image displays a parabola on a Cartesian coordinate plane, clearly labeling its fundamental geometric elements. The blue curve represents the parabola itself. The "Vertex" is indicated as the turning point of the parabola. Inside the curve, the "Focus" is marked, a critical point for defining the parabola. A dashed orange line, labeled "Axis of symmetry", passes vertically through both the vertex and the focus. Below the vertex, a horizontal dashed red line shows the "Directrix". Finally, a horizontal dashed blue line segment passing through the focus and extending to the parabola is identified as the "Latus rectum".

To work with parabolas in the coordinate plane, we consider two cases: those with a vertex at the origin and those with a vertex at a point other than the origin. We begin with the former.

discrepancies: The 'Latus rectum' label sits directly on top of the dark-blue parabola arm at the upper-left (both words overprint the curve and nearly touch the arrowhead), whereas in the source it sits in clear white space to the left of the y-axis with a curved leader arrow into the chord.
The leader arrow from 'Latus rectum' terminates on the parabola arm rather than on the light-blue dashed chord itself, so it reads as pointing at the curve instead of the latus rectum segment.

Composition/proportion differs: the generated drawing leaves a very large empty region below the x-axis (roughly the bottom 40% of the canvas is blank) and pushes the parabola into the upper-left, while the source is tightly cropped around the curve, axes and labels.
The 'Focus' label is placed so the light-blue dashed latus rectum passes through/behind the text; in the source the label is set clear above-right of the dot with no line crossing it.

The latus rectum in the source spans symmetrically a short distance either side of the focus and clearly terminates on the curve; in the generated version the right half of the dashed chord extends past the curve into empty space.
evaluation.notes: Structurally faithful reproduction of the labeled parabola with all six named features, correct colors and dash styles, and a rich, genuinely pedagogical interaction set (p slider, P slider, distance-construction toggle, 6-step demo, hover isolation); the main weaknesses are the 'Latus rectum' label/arrow colliding with the curve, the chord overshooting the parabola, and a loosely cropped composition with excess empty space below the x-axis.

feedback.rationale: The concept and interaction structure are correct (concept 5, interactivity 5); remaining issues are concrete rendering fixes—label placement/leader arrow, chord endpoint clipping, and canvas cropping—which belong to the generator.

demo_steps.title: It holds everywhere
demo_steps.narration: Slide P along the curve. The two segments change length together but never differ — this equality is the definition of the parabola, not a special case.

demo_steps.title: The vertex is the midpoint
demo_steps.narration: Move P to the bottom. Both distances shrink to the same value p: the vertex is the one point sitting halfway between focus and directrix, on the axis of symmetry.

demo_steps.title: Changing p reshapes the curve
demo_steps.narration: Increase p: the focus climbs, the directrix drops the same amount, and the parabola opens out wide with a latus rectum of width 4p.

demo_steps.title: A tight parabola
demo_steps.narration: Shrink p and the focus and directrix squeeze toward the vertex, pinching the curve into a narrow channel — same definition, different single parameter.

plan.keyInsight: Every point on a parabola is the same distance from the focus as from the directrix — the vertex is simply the point where that shared distance is smallest, which is why it sits exactly halfway between them.
plan.reconstructionNotes: Cartesian plane with thin black arrowed axes, origin low and left of center; 'x' at the right end of the horizontal axis, 'y' at the top of the vertical axis. A heavy dark-blue (#1f4e79-ish) upward-opening parabola fills the upper portion with arrowheads on both branches. Its vertex is a filled dark-blue dot sitting noticeably above the x-axis, with a short black leader line to a left-side label 'Vertex'. A dashed vertical orange line passes through the vertex from top to bottom of the frame, labeled 'Axis of symmetry' in orange near the top right of the line. A small teal dot on that line a short way above the vertex is labeled 'Focus' in teal to its right. A dashed light-blue horizontal chord through the focus stretches from one branch to the other; a curved black arrow points to it from the blue label 'Latus rectum' at the upper left. Below the vertex, a dashed red horizontal line spans the full frame width and is labeled 'Directrix' in red at its right end, positioned between the vertex and the x-axis. Keep vertex-to-focus and vertex-to-directrix gaps visually identical. In the 'Distance construction' view, dim the text labels, place a highlighted point P on one branch, draw a teal straight segment P→focus and a red vertical segment P→directrix with a small right-angle marker at the directrix, mark both with equal tick marks and an '=' callout, and show small 'p' brackets between vertex-focus and vertex-directrix. Hover should brighten the chosen feature and gray the others.

discrepancies: The 'Vertex' leader line in the source ends in a small arrowhead pointing at the vertex dot; the generated version draws a plain line with no arrowhead.

The light-blue latus rectum in the generated figure extends a few pixels past the parabola on the right side (and is drawn slightly wider than the chord endpoints on the curve), whereas in the source it terminates cleanly at/inside the curve.
Minor composition difference: the generated parabola's arms rise slightly higher/wider relative to the frame than in the source, and the directrix segment is shorter relative to the plotted width.
evaluation.notes: A near drop-in replacement for the source: correct curve, vertex/focus/directrix/axis-of-symmetry/latus-rectum geometry, matching colours and all five annotations legibly placed, plus a genuinely useful p slider, PF=PD construction toggle, P slider and 6-step guided demo; only tiny geometric slips (missing arrowhead on the vertex leader, latus rectum overshooting the curve).
action_items: Add a small arrowhead at the end of the 'Vertex' leader line so it points at the vertex dot as in the source.
Clamp the latus rectum endpoints exactly to the curve (x = h ± 2p) and verify at all p values that the dashed chord does not overshoot the parabola.

Tighten the default framing slightly (reduce arm rise / widen directrix) so proportions match the source crop more closely, and align the 'Distance construction view' checkbox inline with its text label.
